chunks: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Asimi, from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Sulami, from Ali ibn Asbat, from al-Hakam ibn Miskin, from Jamil ibn Darraj, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'When a male slave marries a free woman, their children are free; and when a free man marries a female slave, their children are free.'
ai.seo_question: What is the legal status of children born from a marriage between a slave and a free person in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the juristic principle that in mixed-status unions, the child inherits the free status of the free parent, ensuring social mobility and legal clarity for offspring. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the emancipation of the mother (*Umm al-Walad*) often accompanying these marriages, thereby securing the freedom of the entire lineage. This ruling is pivotal in distinguishing between the status of the parents and the resulting children, preventing the perpetuation of slavery within the family unit when one parent is free.
